references.text: Aaron shall speak to the people on Moses' behalf and be as a mouth for him, while Moses shall be as God to Aaron. This verse establishes the prophetic relationship between Moses and Aaron.
The Lord appoints Aaron as spokesman for Moses, and Moses is to put the words in his mouth. This prepares for the roles described in 7:1.
The psalm uses the term 'gods' (elohim) for human judges or leaders, which sheds light on the use of 'elohim' for Moses in relation to Pharaoh.
The promise of a prophet like Moses whom the Lord will raise up. Aaron as Moses' prophet points forward to this prophetic ministry.
Jeremiah is appointed as a prophet to the nations, similarly to how Moses was set as 'god' over Pharaoh with authority to speak God's words.
Jesus quotes Psalm 82:6 and explains that Scripture calls those to whom God's word came 'gods'. This clarifies how Moses could be called 'elohim' for Pharaoh.
The continuation of the verse explaining that Moses is to speak all that God commands, and Aaron is to speak to Pharaoh. This elaborates on the prophetic relationship.
Moses' role as God's spokesman in Exodus anticipates and points directly forward to the great prophet he himself foretells in this text.
Repetition of the prophecy about 'one like me', confirming that Moses' authority in Exodus points toward a greater fulfillment.
